assembly_notes:
Demonstration gyroscope. The object is authored in a chain of ring-local frames so that the category's one hard invariant is structural rather than incidental: a gimbal member's own trunnion (hold) axis is its local +Z with its pole pins at ±Z, the axis it hands to its child is its local +X, and its band lies in whichever plane contains both of those axes. A pure gimbal ring and an opposed_bearings carrier therefore lie in their local XZ plane; a bearing_spider carrier lies in its local YZ plane, because there the spin axis is the member's own normal. The rotor's spin axis is its local +Z with the flywheel in local XY.

Every joint is solved with mate_axes between an AxisInterface on the parent and one on the child, both anchored at their own frame origin, and registered with register_interface_mate. Because both interface points are the gimbal centre, every joint after the base has origin exactly (0,0,0), and consecutive joint axes come out mutually orthogonal by construction — the authored check 'every gimbal axis passes through the common centre and is orthogonal to its parent' composes the origin rotations and asserts both facts on every seed.

Slots. support_base builds the fixed root and owns the first rotation axis: a weighted cast pedestal, a slender tapered column, a splayed tripod, or a wall bracket whose axis is horizontal (0,-1,0) instead of vertical. ring_stack is two nested members and three joints, or three nested members and four joints with a fourth independent axis; it is a structural slot rather than a multiplicity because the extra member is not a repeat — it adds a distinct axis and re-orients every plane in the stack. ring_section is the member cross-section: flat machined band with an edge bead, round tube hoop with bearing seat rings, or a rectangular window carrier frame for the innermost member. spindle_support is how the carrier captures the rotor: two opposed in-plane pole bearings on a through axle, or one central race on a spider. rotor_form is the flywheel: crowned drum, shaped disc with a proud perimeter band, spoked inertia rim, or plain bevelled solid disc. index_hardware is the outer ring's free pole: plain trunnion stub or slender pointer mast. gimbal_motion is free swing or a mechanically limited swing with real end stops.

Host adaptation. rotor_bore_m is re-derived from whichever carrier the section slot built — the annulus and tube hoops present ring_inner[carrier], while the rectangular cage presents its bar line — and flywheel_radius_m follows it, so a rotor form and a carrier form combine without excluding any pair. The parent's trunnion sleeve starts 4 mm beyond pole_reach_m[k+1], which is the child's furthest material along the shared axis for an annulus, a tube and a cage alike. The spider steps its race back past rotor_back_reach_m, which is per rotor form. The base pushes its azimuth bearing back to mount_station_m so it always clears the outer ring's own bottom pole.

Clearances. Every shaft/bearing fit in the model is a real bore on a 0.6 mm radial running clearance — under the 1 mm assembly-support band, over the tessellation error, and therefore supported by baseline QC without a single ctx.allow_overlap, which the whole source pool relies on. Nested members keep ring_gap_m = max(0.014, 0.10 R) of running clearance, checked against each member's true swept envelope (its furthest material from the gimbal centre, which is rotation-invariant) rather than at neutral only. The rotor axle is capped inside the carrier's envelope instead of the source's 205 mm protruding shaft, which crosses the outer band whenever the tilt joint passes through zero.

outer_ring_radius_m, ring_width_ratio, rotor_radius_ratio and gimbal_rise_m are the honest continuous parameters. There is no multiplicity: the third gimbal member is a structural candidate, and no homogeneous repeat exists across every rotor candidate (the spoked rim's radial members have no counterpart in a plain solid disc, which the source explicitly builds without spokes or cutouts). core_domain = 4 x 2 x 3 x 2 x 4 x 2 x 2 = 768; raw_domain = 768.

derived.name: mount_station_m
derived.rationale: the base pushes its bearing back until it clears whatever ring the section slot built

derived.name: pole_engagement_m
derived.rationale: how deep the outer ring's pole pin runs inside the azimuth bore

derived.name: sleeve_start_m
derived.rationale: the parent's trunnion sleeve starts beyond the child's furthest material on the shared axis, whether the child is an annulus, a tube or a cage

derived.expression: (0,0,1) coplanar | (0,1,0) orthogonal, chosen from ring_stack and spindle_support
derived.name: child_plane_radial
derived.rationale: the parent hands the child the radial that puts the child's plane where its own two axes actually live

derived.name: flywheel_radius_m
derived.rationale: the rotor is sized from the bore the carrier the section slot built actually presents

derived.name: race_offset_m
derived.rationale: the spider steps its race back past whichever rotor form was built

derived.name: pole_face_station_m
derived.rationale: the free pole face moves with whichever cross-section the ring slot built

derived.name: stop_radius_m
derived.rationale: the stop arc clears the azimuth bearing of whatever base is in play

derived.name: stop_block_angle_rad
derived.rationale: block placement solved from the limit and both half widths

candidates.evidence: A broad crowned lathe body 198 mm across and 52 mm tall carries a stepped pedestal collar, upright, satin bearing housing and chrome cap on the vertical axis; the wide low mass and the four-step bearing stack are the recognisable desktop demonstrator support.
candidates.name: weighted_pedestal
candidates.notes: Broad crowned cast body on a ten-station revolved profile with a pedestal collar, an upright and a bored azimuth bearing on the vertical axis. The bore is drilled through the upright so the ring's pole pin runs in it rather than into it.

dimensions.plane_rule: the member's plane always contains its own hold axis; the parent's radial decides whether it is coplanar with or orthogonal to its parent

candidates.name: two_ring_gimbal
candidates.notes: Outer ring plus spindle carrier: four parts, three joints, axes azimuth / tilt / spin. The carrier's plane is handed the parent's own plane, which reproduces the coplanar hoop pair of both source anchors.

parameters.name: outer_ring_radius_m

parameters.name: ring_gap_m
parameters.rationale: running clearance between a member's outer envelope and its parent's bore; it also sets how far a trunnion pin travels before entering its sleeve

parameters.name: ring_outer_m
parameters.rationale: nested outer radii, one per gimbal member

parameters.name: ring_inner_m
parameters.rationale: inner radii; inner members are proportionally lighter, as in the source stack

parameters.name: ring_thick_m
parameters.rationale: band thickness along each member's own normal

parameters.expression: pin[0] = max(0.0035, 0.055 * outer_ring_radius_m); pin[k] = max(0.0030, 0.050 * ring_outer[k])
parameters.name: pole_pin_radius_m
parameters.rationale: trunnion pin radius per member; every bore is this plus the running fit

parameters.expression: ring_outer[k] for an annulus or a tube hoop; carrier_half_pole_m for a carrier frame
parameters.name: pole_reach_m
parameters.rationale: the member's furthest material along its own hold axis; the parent's trunnion sleeve starts 4 mm beyond it so the child can never sweep into it

parameters.expression: 0.82 * ring_outer[carrier] for opposed_bearings | 0.70 * ring_outer[carrier] for bearing_spider
parameters.name: carrier_half_pole_m
parameters.rationale: carrier frame half extent along the hold axis; with the span half extent it keeps the frame's corner diagonal under the carrier's own envelope radius

parameters.expression: 0.55 * ring_outer[carrier] for opposed_bearings | 0.70 * ring_outer[carrier] for bearing_spider
parameters.name: carrier_half_spin_m
parameters.rationale: carrier frame half extent along the spin axis / spider post line

parameters.name: carrier_bar_m
parameters.rationale: carrier frame bar width; source cage uses 8 mm bars on a 70 mm half extent

parameters.expression: ring_inner[carrier] for an annulus or tube hoop | carrier_half_pole_m - carrier_bar_m for an opposed carrier frame | min(half_pole, half_spin) - carrier_bar_m for a spider carrier frame
parameters.name: rotor_bore_m
parameters.rationale: clear radius the flywheel has to live inside; this is the host adaptation that lets a rectangular cage take the same rotor slot as a round hoop

parameters.name: spin_seat_m
parameters.rationale: where the spin bearing sleeve or the spider post meets the carrier body

parameters.name: axle_radius_m
parameters.rationale: spindle radius; every spin bore is this plus the running fit

parameters.name: axle_half_m
parameters.rationale: half length of the through axle. Deliberately capped inside the carrier's own envelope instead of the source's 205 mm protruding shaft, which crosses the outer band whenever the tilt joint passes through zero

parameters.name: race_offset_m
parameters.rationale: axial station of the central race, clear of whichever rotor form the rotor slot built behind the disc

parameters.name: race_len_m
parameters.rationale: length of the spider's central bearing race

parameters.name: bearing_fit_m
parameters.rationale: radial running clearance in every bore in the model. It is under the 1 mm assembly-support band and over the tessellation error, so every pin, trunnion and axle is supported without a single overlap allowance

candidates.evidence: The innermost ring's plane is perpendicular to the spin axis: a small toroidal race is carried at the bore centre by two straight arms spanning the full 102 mm bore and two end posts, and the rotor journal runs in that single central race. A different part tree and a different relationship between ring plane and spin axis.
candidates.name: bearing_spider
candidates.notes: The carrier's plane is perpendicular to the spin axis: two rim posts and two inclined struts carry one central bored race, and the rotor journal runs in it. The struts step back from short rim posts instead of lying flat across the bore, so the spider never reaches outside the carrier's own envelope whatever the rotor size.

parameters.name: rotor_radius_ratio
parameters.rationale: flywheel radius as a fraction of the innermost member's clear bore less its running clearance; source ratios are 0.055/0.075 = 0.73 and 0.097/0.1065 = 0.91
